newsitem.title: FRANCE: French insurer Axa reports strong profit rise.
newsitem.headline: French insurer Axa reports strong profit rise.

text.p: Axa, which is merging with rival French insurer UAP to create the world's second largest insurer, reported on Wednesday that 1996 profits grew 39.5 percent to 3.81 billion francs ($670.4 million).

UAP, by contrast, announced a 6.45 billion franc loss after taking 7.59 billion francs in exceptional charges as part of a cleanup of its books to prevent its money-losing activities weighing on the new group's future.

Axa and Union des Assurances de Paris are integrating to form Axa-UAP after surprising financial markets last November by announcing that they would combine operations to form a new global financial force.
It was the last time that Axa and UAP, France's two biggest insurers, will produce two separate sets of figures. As of this year, their accounts will be consolidated.
Axa said its performance was driven by life insurance results, due to a strong improvement in the United States, France and the United Kingdom.

The performance was also lifted by property and casualty insurance results which increased strongly in France, Belgium and Britain. The exception was Axa Global Risks in Britain which posted losses due to the strengthening of reserves related to claims which occured prior to 1992.
First time full year consolidation of National Mutual in Australia, consolidated for one month only in 1995, also helped boost profits.

There was a strong increase in net income from U.S. financial services -- DLJ and Alliance Capital Management -- and there was a strong contribution from the holding company thanks to "very good investment results."
There were also extraordinary profits due to changes in local accounting methods in life insuarance at the level of the Dutch and Canadian subisidiaries.

Factors having a negative impact on profits included losses from Axa Leben life insurance unit in German and losses from French real estate subsidiaries due to real estate valuation allowances. ($ = 5.683 French Francs)
